name: parallelogram-angles
title: Parallelogram angles
tagline: Parallelogram from three placed corners; interior angles derived (opposite equal, co-interior 180) plus optional extended-side triangle and diagonal-cevian angle-chase constructs.
description: A single parallelogram ABCD drawn from three placed corners (the fourth is computed so the figure is always a true parallelogram), with any of its interior angles, side lengths, equal-side ticks and diagonals marked, plus two optional angle-chase constructs. The EXTERNAL construct extends one side beyond a corner to a new point and joins it to another corner, forming an attached triangle (the "CBE is a straight line, find angle BAE" figure). The CEVIAN construct drops a line from a corner to a point on a drawn diagonal, deriving the angle where they meet (the "diagonal DB, cevian AE, find angle AEB" figure). You place the corners as a sketch in any units; the model derives every interior angle (opposite angles equal, co-interior angles add to 180), every side length (opposite sides equal), every diagonal length, and the triangle / intersection angles of the two constructs, then auto-fits the figure. Angles are marked by their vertex — a corner's interior angle needs only its vertex; any other angle (an angle inside the attached triangle, the angle a cevian makes with a diagonal, the angle a diagonal makes with a side) is named by its vertex plus the two points its arms run to. Per-element occlusion ("find x" → "?"), highlighting (amber), equal-side ticks, a length unit, a "not to scale" note, an optional caption, and draggable corners on the web. Override any displayed value with a label for the given data of a not-to-scale exam figure. Placed to scale, every derived value equals the true answer, so a reconstruction can be checked against the boxed result.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever the teaching lives on a parallelogram and its angles: naming opposite / co-interior angles, the angle a diagonal makes (alternate angles across the parallel sides), and the classic angle-chase figures where a side is extended past a corner into a triangle, or a diagonal and a second line meet inside the shape. Place THREE consecutive corners as [x, y] points making a sketch, IN ORDER around the perimeter (A, then B, then C); the fourth corner D is computed to close the parallelogram (override its printed letter with fourthLabel). Reference a corner's interior angle by its vertex ({ at: "A" }); reference any other angle by its vertex and the two points its arms reach ({ at: "E", from: "A", to: "B" } marks angle AEB). Reference a side by its two corner labels; a diagonal by its two opposite corners. The model derives every measure, so for a to-scale sketch just mark the element and the right number shows; for a not-to-scale exam figure place a rough parallelogram, set notToScale: true, and override the given values with labels. Common configurations: OPPOSITE / CO-INTERIOR — mark all four interior angles (opposite come out equal, adjacent add to 180), or give one and occlude another. DIAGONAL + ALTERNATE ANGLES — draw a diagonal (diagonals: [{ between: ["A","C"] }]) and mark the two alternate angles it makes with the parallel sides ({ at: "A", from: "B", to: "C" } and { at: "C", from: "A", to: "D" }) — they derive equal. EXTENDED SIDE (attached triangle) — external: { onSide: ["C","B"], by: 3, toVertex: "A", label: "E" } extends side CB beyond B to E and joins A to E; mark the triangle's angles at E, B and A by naming their arms, occlude the unknown. DIAGONAL + CEVIAN — draw the diagonal, then cevian: { from: "A", onDiagonal: ["D","B"], at: 0.55, label: "E" } drops AE onto DB at a fraction along it; mark the intersection angle ({ at: "E", from: "A", to: "B" }) and occlude it. Keep the same parallelogram shape and labels across the blocks of one lesson so pupils track one figure — change only what is given, occluded or highlighted; a chase builds up naturally in stages (bare parallelogram → givens → construction line → the answer). Occlude renders a value as "?"; the element stays drawn. UNITS — set unit: "cm" once to append it to bare-number length labels. EXAM FIGURES with no letters — vertexLabels: false stops the letters printing; addressing still uses A/B/C/D. Synonyms a teacher might use: parallelogram, opposite angles, co-interior angles, allied angles, angles on parallel sides, alternate angles, diagonal of a parallelogram, angle chase, find the missing angle, straight line, exterior angle, not to scale.

vertices.description: THREE consecutive corners of the parallelogram, IN ORDER around the perimeter — A, then B, then C. Each is a point in any units; place them as a SKETCH of the parallelogram you want. The FOURTH corner D is computed (D = A + C − B) so the figure is always a true parallelogram — you never place it. The order fixes the default labels: first corner A, second B, third C (fourth D). Only the shape matters; the model auto-fits the figure to the canvas.

at.description: Position of this corner as [x, y] in your own units (y up). Only the SHAPE matters — the figure is scaled to fit.

label.description: Display name for this corner, drawn just outside it. Defaults to A, B, C by order. Override for different names (then reference this corner by the new label everywhere).

fourthLabel.description: Display name for the computed fourth corner. Default "D". Reference this corner by whatever label you set here.

angles.description: The angles to MARK — an arc + value, or a right-angle square. TWO forms. Interior corner angle: give only `at` (the vertex label) — the angle between the two sides meeting there is derived (opposite corners come out equal, adjacent add to 180). ANY OTHER angle: give `at` plus `from` and `to`, the two points its arms run to — e.g. { at: "E", from: "A", to: "B" } marks angle AEB, { at: "A", from: "D", to: "E" } marks angle DAE. Points may be corners (A, B, C, D), the external point, or the cevian point. The measure is DERIVED; override with `label`. Omit an angle to leave it unmarked.

at.description: The vertex the angle sits at — a corner label, the external point, or the cevian point.

from.description: One arm of the angle: the point the first arm runs to. Omit (with `to`) only for a corner's interior angle, which uses the two adjacent corners automatically.

to.description: The other arm of the angle: the point the second arm runs to. Omit (with `from`) only for a corner's interior angle.

label.description: Override the displayed value — the given measure of a not-to-scale figure ("124°") or an unknown ("x"). Omit to show the measure derived from the sketch.

occlude.description: Render this angle's value as "?" — the "find the missing angle" hook. The arc still shows. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this angle (amber arc + value) — the answer, or the angle in question. Default false.

bare.description: Mark this angle with the arc ONLY — no value text. Use when the figure marks an angle without giving its size. occlude beats bare. Default false.

rightAngle.description: Mark this angle as a right angle: a small square instead of an arc and value. Default false.

sides.description: The parallelogram sides to LABEL with a length and/or tick as equal. Address each by its two corner labels (they must be consecutive corners). The length is DERIVED (opposite sides come out equal); override with `label`. Omit a side to leave it bare.

between.description: The two endpoint corner labels of this side, e.g. ["A","B"] (order does not matter). Must be a genuine side — two consecutive corners.

label.description: Override the displayed length — the given value ("8 cm", "x"). Omit to show the derived length.

occlude.description: Render this side's length as "?" — the "find the missing side" hook. The side stays drawn. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to this side (amber). Default false.

ticks.description: Draw this many small equal-length ticks across the side. Sides with the SAME tick count read as equal (opposite sides of a parallelogram). Omit for no tick.

diagonals.description: Diagonals to DRAW — a straight line between two OPPOSITE corners (["A","C"] or ["B","D"]). The length is DERIVED; show it with showLength, occlude it, highlight it, or override with a label. A diagonal is needed for the alternate-angle figure (mark the two alternate angles it makes with the parallel sides) and for the cevian construct (the cevian meets a drawn diagonal). Omit for a plain parallelogram. At most two.

between.description: The two OPPOSITE corner labels this diagonal joins, e.g. ["A","C"] or ["B","D"] (order does not matter).

label.description: Override the displayed length ("8 m", "x"). Omit to leave the diagonal unlabelled unless showLength / occlude is set.

occlude.description: Render the diagonal's length as "?". The line still shows. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the eye to the diagonal and its length (amber). Default false.

showLength.description: Show the derived length even with no label. Default false — a bare diagonal draws just the line.

external.description: ONE external point on an extended side, forming an attached triangle — the "CBE is a straight line, find angle BAE" figure. The side is extended beyond one of its corners to a new point, which is then joined to another corner. Mark the triangle's angles through `angles` (naming their arms, e.g. { at: "E", from: "A", to: "B" }). Omit for no external construct.

onSide.description: The side to extend, named in the DIRECTION of extension: [from, through]. The new point sits beyond the SECOND corner. ["C","B"] extends side CB out past B (so C, B and the new point are a straight line, in that order).

by.description: How far beyond the second corner the new point sits, as a distance in your own units (the same units as the vertices). Positive.

toVertex.description: Which corner to JOIN the new point to, drawing the third side of the attached triangle (e.g. "A" draws the line from A to the new point).

label.description: Display name for the new external point (e.g. "E"). Reference it by this label in `angles`. Default "E".

cevian.description: ONE cevian meeting a diagonal at an interior point — the "diagonal DB, cevian AE with E on DB, find angle AEB" figure. A line is drawn from a corner to a point ON a diagonal; the angle where they meet is derived. Draw the diagonal too (in `diagonals`) so the figure reads. Mark the intersection angle through `angles` ({ at: "E", from: "A", to: "B" }). Omit for no cevian.

from.description: The corner the cevian starts from (e.g. "A").

onDiagonal.description: The two opposite corners of the diagonal the cevian lands on, e.g. ["D","B"] (order sets the direction of `at`: 0 at the first corner, 1 at the second).

at.description: Where on the diagonal the cevian meets it, as a fraction from the first named corner (0) to the second (1). 0.5 is the midpoint.

label.description: Display name for the meeting point (e.g. "E"). Reference it by this label in `angles`. Default "E".

unit.description: The figure's length unit ("cm", "m", "mm"). Appended to every length label that is a BARE NUMBER — a derived length or a purely numeric authored label ("12" → "12 cm"). A label with any other text ("12 cm", "x") is shown verbatim. Angle labels never take it. Default "" (labels stay bare).

vertexLabels.description: Whether to PRINT the corner letters. Set false for exam figures drawn without letters — addressing still uses the default A/B/C/D (and construct labels); only the printing is suppressed. Default true.

notToScale.description: Print a "Not to scale" note by the figure. Only when the source figure prints one. Default false.

caption.description: An optional line of text centred below the figure — the rule or fact being taught, e.g. "Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal". Omit for none.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

draggablePoints.description: Web-only. Let pupils drag a corner (A, B or C) to reshape the parallelogram; the fourth corner, every derived angle, and both constructs recompute live. Best on a to-scale figure (no overridden labels). Default false.
